caveats: Rows are in the library's stored order, by precursor_index, not by m/z: mzLib's own MslLibrary.GetAllEntries enumerates in ascending precursor m/z instead. Sort on precursor_mz for that order.

retention_time is iRT for some precursors and run minutes for others: read retention_time_unit on each row (MslLibraryEntry.RtIsCalibrated). A library can hold both, so never plot or compare the column without it. There is no conversion: iRT becomes minutes only through a calibration against a run.
The library is unfiltered: decoys (D, ED) and entrapment precursors (ET, ED) are rows. Filter on is_decoy, or on decoy_contaminant_target, before counting targets.

A retention_time of 0 may mean the source had none: MslLibraryEntry.FromLibrarySpectrum, the path mzLib converts a text library through, writes RetentionTime ?? 0.0, and mzLib documents no sentinel for it, so 0 is passed through as a value.
nce is a whole number: the format stores NCE x 10 and MslReader reads it back with integer division, so an NCE of 27.5 reads as 27.

A library converted from a text library (.msp) has no NCE, dissociation type, q-value, ion mobility or protein: LibrarySpectrum has no field for them, and MslLibraryEntry.FromLibrarySpectrum fills mzLib's not-available defaults, so nce and q_value are null and dissociation_type is Unknown.

precursor_mz, retention_time and ion_mobility are stored as 32-bit floats and widened to double by mzLib, so 465.74 reads back as 465.739990234375. The extra digits are the float, not a measurement; round them for display.
offset and limit count PRECURSORS. With fragments, each precursor gives one row per fragment ion.
